prose:
pwn.ai presents Upload2Shell as a Ghostscript Type 1 font-loader use-after-free that can escape the interpreter's safety boundary. Its disclosure index follows the same rendering component through print queues, email previews and upload pipelines, while distinguishing confirmed execution from merely tracing a route to Ghostscript. The directly fetched article is substantially fuller than the automated cache excerpt.

The researcher's matrix describes different access conditions for each application. A public upload route is not equivalent to an authenticated upload, and reaching a renderer is not itself proof of command execution in every product. The page identifies upstream and distribution fixes, but these remain the publisher's reported versions and trials here, not an independent advisory audit or reproduction. Separate Ghostscript findings involving other production services must not be conflated with this CVE.
highlights: Underlying component is Ghostscript's font loader
Print, preview and upload routes have different prerequisites
Application matrix distinguishes execution from source-mapped reachability
Some paths require particular plugins or configurations
Publisher identifies Ghostscript 10.08.0 as an upstream fix
Distribution backports use their own version identifiers
Other production-service findings have separate roots
No proof of concept or exploit was executed
